rules: Struktur Email Formal: Subject line yang jelas -> Salam formal (Dear Mr./Ms. + nama keluarga) -> Paragraf pembuka (tujuan email) -> Isi utama (2-3 paragraf singkat) -> Penutup sopan (Thank you for your time/consideration) -> Sign-off formal (Yours sincerely/Best regards) -> Nama lengkap dan jabatan

Frasa Pembuka Formal: 'I am writing to inquire about/regarding...' (untuk pertanyaan), 'I am writing to inform you that...' (untuk pemberitahuan), 'Thank you for your email dated...' (untuk balasan), 'Further to our conversation...' (follow-up)

Frasa Permintaan Sopan: 'I would appreciate if you could...' (sangat formal), 'Could you please...' (formal), 'Would it be possible to...' (meminta kemungkinan), 'I would be grateful if...' (mengungkapkan terima kasih di awal). Contoh: 'I would appreciate if you could send me the updated proposal by Friday.' atau 'Could you please confirm your attendance at the meeting?'

Lampiran dan Referensi: 'Please find attached...' (untuk file terlampir), 'As discussed...' (merujuk pembicaraan sebelumnya), 'With reference to...' (merujuk dokumen/email lain). Contoh: 'Please find attached the quarterly report for your review.'

Penutup Profesional: Gunakan 'Yours sincerely' jika Anda tahu nama penerima (Dear Mr. Smith), gunakan 'Yours faithfully' jika tidak tahu nama (Dear Sir/Madam). Alternatif modern: 'Best regards', 'Kind regards' untuk hampir semua situasi formal. Hindari 'Cheers', 'Thanks', atau 'See you' dalam konteks sangat formal.

commonTrap.trapTitle: Using Informal Registers in Professional Emails

blueprintItems.title: Step 1: Clear Subject Lines and Formal Salutations
blueprintItems.formula: Subject: [Topic Summary] + Dear [Title and Last Name],
blueprintItems.example: Subject: Inquiry Regarding Quarterly Marketing Report, Dear Mr. Harrison,

blueprintItems.title: Step 2: Purpose and Main Body Paragraphs
blueprintItems.formula: Opening Purpose Statement + Supporting Details + Polite Call to Action
blueprintItems.example: I am writing to inquire about the schedule for the upcoming client presentation. Could you please send the updated slides by Thursday?

blueprintItems.title: Step 3: Professional Sign-Offs
blueprintItems.formula: Closing Phrase + Full Name + Job Title

mechanicsRules.rule: Use formal titles such as Mr., Ms., or Dr. followed by the family name in professional salutations.
mechanicsRules.badExample: Dear John, please look at this file.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Dear Ms. Davis, please review the attached file.
mechanicsRules.why: Using first names without prior acquaintance is considered too informal in standard British and international business contexts.

mechanicsRules.rule: Always separate clauses with appropriate punctuation and avoid run-on sentences in formal correspondence.
mechanicsRules.badExample: I am writing to inform you about the delay we had some issues with logistics.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: I am writing to inform you about the delay. We encountered some issues with logistics.
mechanicsRules.why: Clear sentence boundaries ensure that business readers understand your message quickly and without confusion.

mechanicsRules.rule: Capitalize proper nouns, department names, and specific document titles in professional emails.
mechanicsRules.badExample: please send the annual report to the human resources department.
mechanicsRules.goodExample: Please send the Annual Report to the Human Resources Department.
mechanicsRules.why: Proper capitalization demonstrates attention to detail and maintains professional standards.

practicumQuestions.instruction: Transform this direct question into a modal-based formal request:

practicumQuestions.explanation: 'Therefore' effectively links a cause to its resulting consequence in formal professional texts.

pillars.name: Syllable Stress

pillars.name: Polite Intonation

pillars.explanation: Use a warm, controlled tone to sound professional yet approachable during workplace discussions.

stressPairs.shiftExplanation: Notice how the stress shifts to the final syllable in the noun form inquiry.
The primary stress moves to the penultimate syllable when adding the suffix ation.
Stress moves forward to the fourth syllable in the noun form.
